title: Magnetoelectric Sensors for Movement Detection and Analysis
summary: In the study presented here, we will measure gait and balance using CE-certified 3D motion analysis systems, as well as electromagnetic sensors. These electromagnetic sensors have been developed within the SFB 1261 at the Christian-Albrechts-Universität zu Kiel. These small sensors can be integrated into clothing, e.g. a jacket, to measure movements of the upper extremities. The use of these sensors for neurological purposes has already been exempted from the obligation to obtain approval (see BfArM review). The measurement method is complementary to that of 3D motion analysis and the use of this sensor technology would allow us to capture a previously uncovered aspect (i.e., "relative" extent of motion of one body part compared to another, as opposed to 3D motion analysis systems that determine the "absolute" extent of motion) of human motion. There is no direct interaction between the different sensor systems. In addition, the electromagnetic sensors are electrically isolated from the outside, so that no direct contact with conductive components is possible. A gait analysis is performed which examines the characteristics of walking. During gait analysis, for example, step length, walking speed, step frequency, arm swing and joint angle are evaluated. The subject's gait can be reconstructed in the three spatial dimensions and in time. The results of both systems are then compared with each other.
conditions: persons suffering from neurological movement disorders

interventions.name: Subjects will be evaluated once in the movement laboratory. A 3D motion capture system, inertial measurment units and ME-sensors are complementary

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Ability to walk independently with or without walking aids
18 years and older
Exclusion criteria:
- High fall risk (i.e., >2 falls during the last month reported by the participant)
- Any impairment that keeps the participant from giving consent to participate in this study
- Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA) < 15
- Pregnancy as reported by the participant
